correctness.rationale: The all-parameter proof first forces the scattered subsequence \(b(a^{n-1}b)^{n-2}\) in every reset word of the first factor by counting each initial trajectory’s special-state defect visits modulo the size. Relabeling produces the complementary required subsequence. Each common subsequence of these patterns obeys two precise run-skipping inequalities, giving an exact longest-common-subsequence length \(2(n-2)\). The common-supersequence lower bound is matched by explicit words for the three small sizes and by a closed-form all-size witness for sizes at least five. Each image-set invariant is calculated from the actual transition maps. Complete subset-pair BFS independently verifies the exact threshold for sizes two through nine, and direct transition plus LCS routines corroborate the symbolic steps through fifty and thirty states respectively. These experiments do not substitute for the universal argument.

value.rationale: Synchronous-product shortest reset length is a natural invariant in automata and control of multiple devices. Swapping which input performs the rotation or defect destroys alignment of two individually extremal factors. This proof gives a sharp formula for every state size and a precise linear saving relative to the generic sum bound. The forced-pattern LCS lower bound plus all-size constructive attainment addresses a substantive joint-control gap, rather than a routine single-machine substitution or isolated numerical table.
